messages:
harry: quick RFC follow-up — proposing per-tenant opt-in for compat shims instead of a global flip. brief sync?

maya: sounds safer. do you plan control-plane metadata + gateway-inserted header, or client-side header?

harry: control-plane metadata + gateway header. avoids client churn and lets us target tenants.

joel: main worry is cache fragmentation. if we change tokenization or embedding dims, runtime cache keys diverge and hit rate drops.

maya: agree. suggest we include compat version in cache key during canary so hits are explicit. downside: more cache entries.

harry: alternative is edge translation (gateway normalizes payload to runtime shape). preserves runtime cache but adds latency and rollout ordering complexity.

ops-bot: operational note: if cache entries double, GPU memory could spike. recommend autoscale guard rails for canary.

arch-bot: telemetry suggestion: tag requests with compat.opt_in and emit cache_hit_rate_by_compat, p95_by_compat, tokens_per_req_delta.

joel: proposal: short-term control-plane opt-in + compat tag in cache key, 2-week canary on 3 tenants with mixed QPS. measure metrics; if cache hit drops > 20% or mem > 12% pivot to gateway translation.

maya: +1. also require audit log entries when toggling opt-in (enterprise compliance).

harry: implementation notes: add tenant.compat_opt_in: version (string), expires_at (ISO). gateway adds X-RW-Compat header.

joel: action items: joel -> cost + mem impact estimate; maya -> telemetry dashboards and alerts; harry -> gateway header read + RFC doc for edge-translation fallback. aim to start canary next Wednesday.

harry: thanks all. i'll draft the RFC and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
